t: Nothing of the Theatre survives, but this is where it stood in Shoreditch, just outside the City. Built in 1576, it was the first permanent playhouse in England built purely for plays. James Burbage built it, and the Lord Chamberlain's Men played here, with Shakespeare as actor and playwright. John Brayne, a grocer, helped finance it and was to have half of it, but the cost bankrupted him. After his death his widow Margaret fought Burbage in court for that half. The papers from her case tell us much about how early playhouses looked and ran. The timbers later went into the Globe.
